Checked handwritten date, typed salutation, opening paragraph, introduction, all seven correction lines and every numerical fill-in, each mathematical glyph and alphabet, second-group heading, full final paragraph, pencil marginal words and underlines and vertical bar, typed closing, handwritten autograph, all blank margins, and lower-left archive 8. notes.text: Letter dated 16 Juillet, with a final dot and no year on the sheet. It addresses Cher Grothendieck and sends la nouvelle rédaction de 4.10.6. The lower-left 8 is recorded as an archive sheet number, not an author page number.
notes.basis: Observed date at upper right, salutation and opening paragraph, lower-left corner.

notes.text: The letter supplies seven corrections: four following the reference to n° 9 of S.G.A 4 IV, and three after Dans les n° 10 et suivant. Numerical references, E-primes, join sign, Hom arguments and E subscript, handwritten sigma, and script H with A subscript were checked against ink. No cited page or mathematical assertion was checked externally.
notes.basis: Observed correction list; transcription inspection only.

notes.text: The writer says n° 14, Modules sur un topos défini par recollement, is absent from the notes received, recalls drafting it and thinks it was handed over: je pense bien te l'avoir donné. The final source sentence is J'espère que ce numéro ne s'est pas perdu. These are the writer's recollection and concern, not verified facts about the transmission.

The pencil note reads demander on the first underlined line and Messing on the second. No separate à is visible. Its vertical bar stands immediately to the right of the note and to the left of the typed paragraph; the transcription keeps that marginal placement. No attribution of the pencil hand is made.
notes.basis: Half a and one rotated margin crop.

notes.text: No mathematical proof checking was performed. Mathematical context was followed only to notice the membership-like sign and ensure that its uncertainty was not resolved by expectation.
notes.basis: Reading method, not a proof or computation.

notation.evidence: Half a shows one prime after first E, two after the second E, a handwritten downward-pointed two-stroke join sign, equality, then E. Each typed E was inspected separately and has no clearly separate doubled vertical stroke.
The cropped sign has curved upper and lower terminals and a faint central stroke; both visible candidates remain possible.
Half a and crop show a single typewritten H, then om, a lowercase e with uppercase E below, a comma and uppercase G inside round parentheses. No double-struck alphabet is established.
Half a shows a small loop with a rightward upper extension in the typist's blank between foncteur and composé.
Half a shows an ornate handwritten looped H followed by typed om and a typed uppercase A below the baseline.
Half a was checked capital by capital: ordinary typewritten S, G, A, I and V; two full stops are after S and G; the 4 is handwritten.
